rewrites.//: A single segment on purpose. `/c/{id}` is the public front page and the only address whose HTML has to carry its own meta tags; `/c/{id}/submit` and the admin tabs stay static files off the CDN, because nobody should pay a function invocation to open a form. Ordered before the catch-all: the first matching rewrite wins.

headers.//: Hosting defaults HTML to max-age=3600. A deploy replaces the hashed assets, so for the next hour a returning visitor can hold an index.html naming files that no longer exist — which renders as a blank page, not an error. Assets keep the default: their names change with their contents. Every address the shell is served at needs its own entry, because headers match the request path and a rewritten one no longer ends in .html — that is why the list grew when routing moved off the hash.
Not `/c/**`: that would cover `/c/{id}`, which `cfpPage` serves with a Cache-Control of its own, and a header set here wins over one set by the function.
